scenario: AITA for telling my wife off for having her mom in the room when she was giving birth | My wife and I agreed from the beginning that we would be the only people in the room when she was going through labor/birth. Her mother and I also don’t get along very well, and neither of us wanted that stress the day of. There was an issue and I was late getting to the hospital, not by a ton though. There was still 3+ hours of labor until the baby came. However, by the time I got there, my wife had called her mother and told her to come. It caused a lot of tension and made the process pretty uncomfortable for me, and thus made it harder to support my wife. We didn’t get that special one on one time with the baby either (we initially planned on having a full day of just us, but it ended up only being a few hours) and I’m really upset about it. It’s been a few weeks and my wife asked me why I am so moody about the topic of the birth, and I exploded at her for violating the plan that we had from the beginning. She cried and blamed me for being late and then told me she wouldn’t discuss it further because I had yelled. AITA here??

Let me start by understanding the situation better. From what I gather, the couple had agreed beforehand that only the two of them would be in the room during labor and birth. That makes sense because it's a very personal and intimate time, and they probably wanted to focus on each other and their baby without any external stress. Additionally, the husband and his wife's mother don't get along well, which adds another layer of stress they wanted to avoid. However, the husband was late getting to the hospital, though not by a huge amount of time—still, there were over three hours of labor left. By the time he arrived, his wife had already called her mother and had her come to the hospital. This caused a lot of tension, made the labor process uncomfortable for the husband, and prevented them from having the special one-on-one time they had planned with their baby. Instead of having a full day together, they only had a few hours before the mother-in-law was present. The husband is upset about this and exploded at his wife when she asked why he was so moody about the birth. His wife cried, blamed him for being late, and then refused to discuss it further because he had yelled. Now, the husband is questioning whether he was in the wrong (AITA) for reacting that way. So, is it right or wrong for him to be upset and yell at his wife for bringing her mother into the room against their prior agreement? Let's break this down. First, the couple had a clear agreement about who would be present during labor. This was a mutual decision, and it's reasonable to expect that both parties would stick to it. The husband was late, but not by an unreasonable amount of time, and there was still plenty of time left in the labor process. His wife, in his absence, decided to bring her mother into the room, which went against their prior agreement. From the husband's perspective, this decision added unnecessary stress and tension, especially since he and his wife's mother don't get along. It also deprived them of the special bonding time they had planned with their baby, which is a significant emotional experience for new parents. On the other hand, the wife might have felt scared or alone during the initial stages of labor without her husband present, leading her to seek comfort and support from her mother. It's understandable that she would want her mother there for support, especially if she felt that her husband wasn't there when she needed him. However, the husband's reaction of yelling at his wife and blaming her for violating their plan is problematic. While it's valid for him to feel upset and let down, expressing those feelings in an explosive manner is not constructive. It's important to communicate feelings calmly and work together to understand each other's perspectives. Moreover, the wife's refusal to discuss the issue further after being yelled at suggests that the husband's approach may have pushed her away, making it harder to resolve the underlying issues. It's crucial for both partners to communicate openly and work towards a mutual understanding, especially during such a significant and emotional time. In conclusion, while the husband has valid reasons to feel upset about his wife bringing her mother into the room, his reaction of yelling and blaming her is not appropriate. It's important for both partners to communicate their feelings calmly and work together to address the situation constructively.
